tasks.short: Direct which animals breed, and record the mating and the offspring.

steps.what: Choose parents against the breeding goal.
Record the mating, the date and the animals.
Judge the offspring against the same goal.
Update the herd book with the selection.

tasks.design: Matings and offspring are fields on the herd book in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The farm manager still chooses the parents and still judges the offspring. The book updates only from that selection note.
tasks.previous_blocker: The herd book was a workbook the manager trusted and nobody else could update without asking.
tasks.enabler_now: Animal, date, sire, dam and outcome are a fixed list a form can store.
tasks.still_hard: Which line is improving is still a judgement over seasons, not one litter.
tasks.human_edge: The manager holds the breeding goal and can see a line going the wrong way.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes on the book. Choosing parents and judging offspring stay. The manager does not hand the goal to a score.

reach.learn: Which animals are in the current plan

evidence.claim: A herd book with required fields stops a mating record that names no animals. It does not rank breeding value.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager sets the breeding goal and the selection. Workers record events. A genetic evaluation, if any, is a specialist's report the manager reads, not a score that decides.
Structured input: animal id, sire, dam, date, outcome. Producer is the worker at the event. An unknown animal id is rejected.
No automated ranking of animals is in this design.
unknowns: Is there a herd book with stable animal ids?
Who may change the breeding goal?
research_questions: How often is a recorded sire later corrected?

already_counted.description: Judging offspring is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire animal ids when stock is sold.

approvals.approved_version: selection note the manager wrote for those offspring

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If animal identities are not stable, the book cannot update itself and only the blank form helps. Judgement stays. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Negotiate sale, storage or shipment of a crop or of livestock.

steps.what: Prepare the lot: quantity, grade and cost.
Negotiate price, storage and shipment with the buyer.
Write the agreed terms into a short contract note.

loop.input: the lot sheet and the terms the manager typed after the call
loop.output: a contract note that quotes only those terms
loop.check: price, quantity and date must match what was typed; else no note
loop.stop: one draft; if a term was not typed, leave it blank
loop.why_not_simpler: the commercial terms are not a template; only the sentence shape is

steps.what: Sign the note or send it back.

tasks.design: The lot sheet is filled from the accepted log in {OPS_SYSTEM}: quantity, grade, lot. The negotiation stays a call or a meeting. A draft note is kept only when price, quantity and date match what the manager typed after the call. Signature is on {ESIGN} for that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lot was rebuilt from memory before each call, and the agreed price lived in a mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Quantity and grade are already on the accepted log, so the sheet is a query. The draft can be checked against typed terms.
tasks.still_hard: The buyer’s willingness, and what storage is really available, come out in the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows what the lot will cost to hold, and when to walk away.
tasks.altitude: Preparing the lot shrinks. The conversation and the signature stay. The manager gains no right to close a deal they did not agree.

reach.task: Book the haul once terms are signed
reach.learn: Which note is signed and which price is still verbal

evidence.claim: A lot sheet from recorded quantity and grade is deterministic. A price agreed on a call is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager negotiates and signs. Dispatch books transport only from signed terms. The buyer is the other party.
Structured input: lot, quantity, grade, price, currency, storage, ship date. Producer of quantity and grade is the accepted log. Price is typed by the manager after the call, never inferred.
The call is most of the task and stays.
unknowns: Who may sign a sale, and up to what value?
Are grades already a controlled list?
research_questions: How often does a signed price get renegotiated before shipment?

already_counted.description: Reading and signing the note is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Keep grade names aligned with what buyers use.

approvals.approved_version: draft terms version the manager signs; an edit voids the signature

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If grades are not on the log, the lot sheet is still typed. The call does not shrink. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose brood stock and keep the living register of those animals.

steps.what: Score candidate stock against the written criteria.
Write the score and the decision onto the register.
Cull, treat or keep, and say why.
Carry out the daily care of the kept stock.

tasks.design: Criteria stay a document the farm manager owns. Scores and keep-or-cull decisions are fields on the brood register in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Daily care of kept stock stays with the technician. A cull is posted only with the manager's reason.
tasks.previous_blocker: Brood lists were a notebook, so a fish culled last month was still on the spawn plan.
tasks.enabler_now: A register with identity, score and status removes the second list.
tasks.still_hard: Condition of a live animal is seen in the hand, not in the last score.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can refuse a candidate the numbers like.
tasks.altitude: The notebook chase shrinks. Scoring and the cull stay. The manager does not delegate the cull to a threshold.

reach.task: Care for the kept brood stock
reach.learn: Which animals are in, and which cull is signed

evidence.claim: A status field stops a culled animal staying on the spawn list. The score itself is the manager's.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager scores and decides. Technicians care for stock. A threshold does not cull.
Structured input: animal id, score, date, decision, reason. Producer is the manager at the tank. A missing reason blocks a cull.
Technician care time is not this role's.
unknowns: What reason codes does the site already use?
research_questions: How often is a kept animal later found unfit?

already_counted.description: The keep-or-cull decision is already remaining time.

incremental.description: Revise criteria after a poor spawning season.

approvals.approved_version: score and reason the manager records for that animal

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Identification that is not individual keeps this on paper. The decision stays anyway. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read soil results and set the fertiliser the crop actually needs.

steps.what: Take the soil samples on the named blocks.
File the laboratory result against the block.
Calculate a rate from the result and the crop.
Change the rate for this block and this season.
Issue the fertilizer application order for that decision.

tasks.design: Laboratory figures are filed against the block. A rate table on {DATA_PLATFORM} proposes kilos per hectare from those figures and the crop. The farm manager changes the rate, and {OPS_SYSTEM} issues an application order only for that decision. Sampling stays physical.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results arrived as a PDF and were retyped into a fertiliser workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: A result with a block id and a nutrient is enough for a rate table. The PDF still needs a person if it will not parse.
tasks.still_hard: A waterlogged block or a crop under stress is not in the rate table.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which block should not get the table's rate this season.

ambition.what: Set a rate for every sampled block in the week the result arrives, not at the next monthly meeting.

tasks.altitude: Retyping results shrinks. Sampling and the seasonal adjustment stay. The manager can still cut a rate to zero.

reach.learn: Which rate was adjusted, and which order is current

evidence.claim: A rate from a soil figure and a crop table is arithmetic. Adjusting it for the season is not.
Fertiliser use can be limited by national environmental rules. The source pack does not name the farm rule, so the order stays a signed decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager signs the rate. Workers apply it. The laboratory produces the result. Environmental limits are checked by the manager, not assumed in the table.

Structured input: block, nutrient, value, unit, crop, rate, unit. Producer of the value is the laboratory file. A file that will not yield those fields is typed. No rate is invented for a missing value.
unknowns: Do laboratory files already name the block?
Which nutrients does the site actually apply?
research_questions: How often does the manager cut a table rate to zero?

already_counted.description: Adjusting the rate is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Update the rate table when a crop or a limit changes.

approvals.approved_version: fertiliser decision for that block; a changed rate voids the order

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If results stay unstructured, someone still types them. Sampling does not shrink. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Breeding, sales, brood stock and fertiliser rates keep a person on the judgement. Books, lot sheets and rate arithmetic shrink. Signature stays on the manager.
reach: Workers record events against animal and block ids.
Sales book haul only from signed terms.
skills_to_grow: Separate a recorded fact from a breeding or rate decision.
Type a price after the call rather than hoping a note infers it.
role.ambitious_version: Every sale note ties to a lot, and every fertiliser order ties to a rate the manager adjusted.

job.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
